goal: Add a bounded remote-only worker continuity contract so disposable Agents automatically recover an interrupted pushed handoff at the next invocation before accepting a new task, preserve the five-level goal hierarchy, and develop in parallel without creating a second semantic control plane.
baseline_impact: none; this extends repository-backed continuity and parallel workstream governance without changing Evidence, PIT/no-lookahead, Reality/Judgment/Outcome, provenance, source authority, or semantic-owner invariants
schema_impact: control-plane JSON and validation only; no product database migration
acceptance: Every worker can recover terminal/long/medium/short/current goals while reading only bounded role and workstream state, and the immediate cursor remains distinct from strategic horizons.

A worker startup preflight derives CLEAN, RECOVERY_REQUIRED, or BLOCKED exclusively from refreshed remote reservation, worker ref, cursor checkpoint, bounded commit delta, and durable receipts; it does not rely on local cache or chat history.

A pushed substantive or WIP checkpoint that lacks its cursor acknowledgment is detected before new work and can be acknowledged honestly as partial or unverified; work never pushed to the remote is explicitly retried from the last declared atomic action rather than claimed as recovered.
Main-owned reservation intent, goal, acceptance, scope, capability owners, dependencies, and assignment fencing cannot be redefined by the worker cursor.

No timer, dialogue count or fixed push cadence is a correctness gate; coherent tasks use remote S checkpoints and cursor-only H acknowledgements, and the next invocation automatically repairs any pushed S that was interrupted before H.

Parallel workers communicate through bounded durable request and completion-receipt pointers, remain within disjoint reservations, and integrate through one serial lane; v1 does not mistake blob existence for semantic request satisfaction.
Hot handoff, router, request, dependency, and cursor state receive explicit size/count bounds so default recovery cost depends on active workstreams rather than project age.

Focused tests cover normal handoff, interrupted-after-push recovery, stale or non-ancestor checkpoints, reservation mismatch, dependency gating, and bounded-growth behavior without weakening Architecture Baseline v1 semantics.
